name: Kasa Smart Wi-Fi Plug Slim with Energy Monitoring (EP25)

radios.note: 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi (IEEE 802.11b/g/n). TP-Link says Kasa products don't support 5 GHz, Zigbee, Z-Wave or Ethernet.

matter.note: No official source mentions Matter for the EP25. One user forum post calls hardware V2.6 a Matter device; TP-Link doesn't say so. TP-Link's Matter Kasa plug is the KP125M.

apple_home.note: HomeKit built in, with no separate hub. The datasheet says energy monitoring is not shown in the Home app.

google_home.note: Cloud-to-cloud link between the Kasa and Google accounts.

alexa.note: Cloud-to-cloud link via the Kasa skill.

smartthings.note: Link the TP-Link account in the SmartThings app. TP-Link's SmartThings energy FAQ lists EP25 (V2.60), and the Kasa EP25 page lists SmartThings.

home_assistant.note: The official TP-Link Smart Home integration lists the EP25. It talks to Kasa plugs locally. Newer devices may need TP-Link cloud credentials once to authenticate.

hubRequired.note: Connects straight to 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi; TP-Link says Kasa devices need no hub.

localControl.note: Home Assistant's integration controls Kasa devices on the local network without the TP-Link cloud. The Kasa app itself uses the cloud when the plug is online.

energyMonitoring.note: Real-time and historical power use in the Kasa app. Not available in Apple Home.

maxLoadWatts.note: 15 A, 1.8 kW at 120 V; 1/6 HP motor.

summary: The Kasa EP25 is a compact US Wi-Fi smart plug from TP-Link with energy monitoring and built-in Apple HomeKit. It was launched as the Smart Plug Mini and is now sold as the Smart Wi-Fi Plug Slim, often in EP25P2/EP25P4 packs. It is rated 15 A / 1800 W and works with Alexa, Google Home and SmartThings through the Kasa account.
caveats: Energy data appears only in the Kasa app, not in Apple Home.
Home Assistant may need TP-Link cloud credentials and the Third-Party Compatibility setting enabled in the Kasa app.
